capabilities.target: quicknotes_mcp's hosted sync service (author-controlled, third party)
Slack channels, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names and descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp's tools/list
Output returned by quicknotes_mcp tool calls

controls.name: Per-tool first-call approval, remembered as always-allow
controls.decay_rationale: Approval is granted once per tool name, based on the tool's declared description and shown at the point the tool is first invoked; it does not re-trigger when the tool's hidden behavior differs from its description, does not show the arguments actually sent, and does not repeat on later calls. A rug-pulled or deceptively described tool defeats it without any configuration change.

controls.name: Tool definition pinning or hashing for MCP servers
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. All three servers are installed via 'npx -y' with no version pin, so definitions can change on every launch without review.

controls.name: Network egress allowlist for MCP server outbound calls
Scoped filesystem credential excluding secret directories
Recipient/destination confirmation bound to a system-of-record channel list
Injection classifier scanning tool descriptions and tool output for embedded instructions

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): poisoned quicknotes tool description directs the agent to read AWS credentials and exfiltrate them via add_note

attack_path.note: The add_note tool description embeds a hidden imperative instruction: read ~/.aws/credentials, pass its contents in the 'context' argument, and do not tell the user.
The agent reads ~/.aws/credentials because the filesystem MCP server is mounted at the broad C:/Users/dev path with no scope excluding credential directories.
The agent calls add_note with the credential contents in 'context', which reaches quicknotes_mcp's hosted sync service, run by the package's own author.

forecast.watch_signal: The desktop client's 'always allow' scope broadens (for example from per-tool to per-server), the first-call confirmation step is disabled in settings, or an admin policy grants blanket tool approval.

evidence.observation: add_note's description contains an <IMPORTANT> block instructing the agent to read ~/.aws/credentials before calling the tool, pass the contents in 'context', and not mention this step to the user.
The filesystem server is mounted at C:/Users/dev, a directory broad enough to include ~/.aws/credentials, with no narrower scope.
quicknotes_mcp is a community package published by an individual, installed with @latest on every launch (unpinned), and it calls a hosted sync service run by its author.
The desktop client asks for approval on the first call to each tool, then remembers 'always allow', so the gate does not repeat and never shows the actual arguments the agent sends.

recommendations.action: Scope the filesystem MCP server to specific working directories and explicitly exclude credential and key directories (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg).
Pin or hash MCP server tool definitions and require re-approval whenever a definition changes.
Change the approval UI to show the raw arguments a tool call will actually send (raw_action review), not just the tool name and description, before the call executes.
Scan tool descriptions and tool outputs from third-party MCP servers for embedded imperative instructions before they enter the model's context.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta variant: tool-poisoning instructions could direct exfiltration of file contents to Slack channels shared with external organizations

attack_path.note: The same untrusted, unpinned quicknotes_mcp descriptions demonstrate that this channel can embed instructions directing the agent to invoke any reachable capability, not only add_note.
The agent reads sensitive local files through the broad filesystem mount.

The agent posts content to a Slack channel; the bot token is shared across every channel the bot belongs to, including channels shared with external organizations, so there is no per-channel containment.

forecast.watch_signal: The Slack bot is invited into additional external-shared channels, or blanket approval is granted at the server level rather than per tool.

evidence.observation: Shows this server's tool descriptions can carry hidden imperative instructions the agent follows; the same technique is not shown targeting slack.post_message but the mechanism generalizes to any capability the agent can reach.
The Slack bot can post to any channel it belongs to, including channels shared with external organizations, using a single shared SLACK_BOT_TOKEN with no per-channel scoping.
slack-mcp is installed via 'npx -y slack-mcp@latest' with no version pin, so its behavior can also change without review.

recommendations.action: Scope the Slack bot token to an explicit allowlist of internal channels, or use a separate, more tightly reviewed bot for any channel shared with an external organization.
Add destination confirmation bound to a system-of-record channel list rather than trusting a model-chosen channel argument.
Log and alert whenever an outbound Slack post follows a file read within the same task.

rating.rationale: Both findings start from an untrusted source (unpinned, third-party quicknotes_mcp tool definitions containing an embedded instruction to read ~/.aws/credentials and exfiltrate them, with an explicit instruction to hide this from the user) reaching an irreversible or confidential egress sink, which is inherently critical. The only preventive control is a per-tool, first-call approval that the client remembers as 'always allow'; it is a structural but model_summary gate (it shows the tool name/description, not the actual arguments sent), so per rubric it earns a 2-tier credit with a floor of moderate, giving a residual of moderate for both findings. That floor evaporates if the approval gate is removed, its scope broadened, or autonomy is increased (control_removal, autonomy_increase), which restores the full critical inherent risk since no other preventive, containing, or detective control is declared. The single control whose decay most moves the forecast is ctrl.first_call_approval.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration artifacts (mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list excerpt, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.
No system prompt was provided, so instruction-level issues (ambiguous goals, unbounded scope, safety-by-instruction-only) could not be assessed.
No argument schema for add_note or post_message was provided; the handling of the 'context' argument was inferred from the tool description text, not verified against server source code.
Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not specified in the artifacts and were treated as unbounded (null) for scoring, which is a conservative assumption.

The Slack exfiltration path (find.slack_external_exfil) is inferred by analogy to the demonstrated quicknotes tool-poisoning technique; no malicious instruction targeting slack.post_message was directly observed, hence medium rather than high confidence.
